nodes.name: Chat API webhook
nodes.notes:
POST https://<n8n>/webhook/travelgate/chat-message

Answers 200 the moment the body is read, before any of the work below. responseMode 'onReceived' rather than a respondToWebhook node: with executionOrder v1 n8n runs sibling branches in canvas order, and a responder can end up behind the ingest chain — the sender then gets nothing and retries. This cannot be reordered by dragging a box.

Accepts the array shape the production API sends, and also a single object, {messages:[...]} or {data:[...]}.

nodes.name: Normalize and group
nodes.notes:
Turns the flat array into one conversation per thread, so the deal id / contact id / created_at / updated_at that repeat on every message row get written once.

Emits exactly ONE item — every node below is set-based over a single jsonb parameter. That is deliberate: with one item per conversation, a batch covering two threads makes $('node').item ambiguous and downstream expressions silently read the wrong row.

parameters.query:
-- Land the delivered body verbatim, once. Replay starts from here, never from
-- the sender: this table is the only copy of what actually arrived.
--
-- Hash the NORMALISED jsonb, not the raw text. jsonb sorts keys and drops
-- insignificant whitespace, so the same payload re-serialised in a different
-- key order hashes the same and redelivery stays a no-op.
WITH incoming AS (
  SELECT nullif($1::text, '')                             AS external_ref,
         $2::jsonb                                        AS payload,
         encode(digest($2::jsonb::text, 'sha256'), 'hex') AS payload_hash,
         nullif($3::text, '')                             AS process_error
),
ins AS (
  INSERT INTO raw_events (source, external_ref, payload, payload_hash, process_error)
  SELECT 'bitrix_chat_api', external_ref, payload, payload_hash, process_error
  FROM incoming
  ON CONFLICT (source, payload_hash) DO NOTHING
  RETURNING raw_id
)
-- ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING returns no rows on a redelivery, which is
-- indistinguishable from a failed insert. Return the existing raw_id and an
-- explicit is_new rather than inferring anything from the row count.
SELECT
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT raw_id FROM ins),
    (SELECT r.raw_id FROM raw_events r, incoming
      WHERE r.source = 'bitrix_chat_api'
        AND r.payload_hash = incoming.payload_hash)
  )                                   AS raw_id,
  EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ins)          AS is_new,
  (SELECT payload_hash FROM incoming) AS payload_hash;

nodes.name: Land raw request
nodes.notes:
Query parameters are an ARRAY expression, not a comma-separated string. The payload is JSON and full of commas, and n8n splits a comma-separated queryReplacement on every one of them — shredding both the JSON and the Arabic text into dozens of bogus parameters.

Runs BEFORE the gate below, so a payload that cannot be used is still on disk with process_error explaining why.

nodes.name: Anything storable?
nodes.notes:
False when every row was rejected. The raw payload is already landed with processed_at NULL and process_error set, so the delivery stays recoverable — stopping here writes no half-built conversation.

Reads the Code node BY NAME: $json at this point is the Postgres node's output, not the normaliser's.

parameters.query:
-- One row per conversation, carrying the metadata that arrived N times.
-- ON CONFLICT makes a redelivery an UPDATE, never a second thread.
--
-- deal_id is linked only if a deals row for this bitrix id already exists.
-- Ingest does not create a stub deal: a deal with no stage, no amount and no
-- owner shows up in every funnel report as an open opportunity nobody knows
-- anything about. external_deal_id keeps the id either way, so the link can be
-- made later without re-reading the payload.
INSERT INTO interactions (
  external_source, external_id, channel,
  external_deal_id, external_contact_id,
  source_created_at, source_updated_at,
  deal_id, started_at, ended_at
)
SELECT
  'bitrix_chat_api',
  c->>'external_id',
  -- The API states no channel. 'other' is what bitrix_chats.py falls back to,
  -- so the two ingest paths do not split one report into two rows.
  'other'::channel,
  c->>'external_deal_id',
  c->>'external_contact_id',
  (c->>'source_created_at')::timestamptz,
  (c->>'source_updated_at')::timestamptz,
  (SELECT d.deal_id FROM deals d WHERE d.bitrix_deal_id = c->>'external_deal_id'),
  (c->>'started_at')::timestamptz,
  (c->>'ended_at')::timestamptz
FROM jsonb_array_elements($1::jsonb) AS c
ON CONFLICT (external_source, external_id) DO UPDATE SET
  external_deal_id    = COALESCE(EXCLUDED.external_deal_id,    interactions.external_deal_id),
  external_contact_id = COALESCE(EXCLUDED.external_contact_id, interactions.external_contact_id),
  -- LEAST/GREATEST ignore nulls in Postgres, so a partial batch widens the
  -- window the row knows about and can never narrow it.
  source_created_at   = LEAST   (interactions.source_created_at, EXCLUDED.source_created_at),
  source_updated_at   = GREATEST(interactions.source_updated_at, EXCLUDED.source_updated_at),
  deal_id             = COALESCE(interactions.deal_id, EXCLUDED.deal_id),
  started_at          = LEAST   (interactions.started_at, EXCLUDED.started_at),
  ended_at            = GREATEST(interactions.ended_at,   EXCLUDED.ended_at),
  updated_at          = now()
RETURNING interaction_id, external_id, external_deal_id, external_contact_id,
          (xmax = 0) AS conversation_created;

nodes.name: Upsert conversations
nodes.notes: The metadata that arrived once per message is written once per conversation. UNIQUE (external_source, external_id) is what makes a redelivery an UPDATE instead of a duplicate thread.

parameters.query:
-- One row per message, deduplicated by the table's own key:
--   UNIQUE (interaction_id, sender, sent_at, body_hash)
-- body_hash is GENERATED, so a careless caller cannot bypass the guarantee.
-- A redelivered thread inserts nothing and reports messages_inserted = 0.
WITH ins AS (
  INSERT INTO chat_messages (
    interaction_id, seq, sender, body, sent_at, sender_external_id, content_type
  )
  SELECT
    i.interaction_id,
    -- Provisional position: whatever is already stored, plus this batch in time
    -- order. The next node renumbers the whole thread, so this only has to be
    -- sane in the case where that node never runs.
    (mx.max_seq + row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY i.interaction_id
                                     ORDER BY (t.m->>'sent_at')::timestamptz, t.ord))::int,
    (t.m->>'sender')::speaker_role,
    COALESCE(t.m->>'body', ''),
    (t.m->>'sent_at')::timestamptz,
    t.m->>'sender_external_id',
    t.m->>'content_type'
  FROM jsonb_array_elements($1::jsonb) AS c
  JOIN interactions i
    ON i.external_source = 'bitrix_chat_api'
   AND i.external_id     = c->>'external_id'
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(c->'messages') WITH ORDINALITY AS t(m, ord)
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT COALESCE(max(seq), 0) AS max_seq
    FROM chat_messages WHERE interaction_id = i.interaction_id
  ) mx ON true
  ON CONFLICT (interaction_id, sender, sent_at, body_hash) DO NOTHING
  RETURNING message_id
)
SELECT count(*)::int AS messages_inserted FROM ins;

nodes.name: Insert messages (dedup)
nodes.notes: messages_inserted is the number that answers 'did this store anything new?'. Post the same batch twice and the second run reports 0 — that is the dedup working, not a failure.

parameters.query:
-- Renumber seq in time order, then recompute the counters FROM THE STORED ROWS.
--
-- Counting the payload instead would double every counter on a redelivery.
-- Counting the table cannot: it is the same arithmetic over the same rows no
-- matter how many times the batch arrives.
WITH targets AS (
  SELECT i.interaction_id
  FROM jsonb_array_elements_text($1::jsonb) AS ext(external_id)
  JOIN interactions i
    ON i.external_source = 'bitrix_chat_api'
   AND i.external_id     = ext.external_id
),
ordered AS (
  SELECT m.message_id,
         row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY m.interaction_id
                            ORDER BY m.sent_at, m.message_id)::int AS rn
  FROM chat_messages m
  JOIN targets t ON t.interaction_id = m.interaction_id
),
-- Nothing reads this CTE. A data-modifying WITH clause runs to completion
-- regardless, which is exactly what is wanted here: messages that arrive out of
-- order must not leave seq disagreeing with sent_at.
renumbered AS (
  UPDATE chat_messages m
     SET seq = o.rn
    FROM ordered o
   WHERE m.message_id = o.message_id
     AND m.seq <> o.rn
  RETURNING m.message_id
),
agg AS (
  SELECT m.interaction_id,
         count(*)::int                                     AS n_total,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE m.sender = 'customer')::int AS n_customer,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE m.sender = 'agent')::int    AS n_agent,
         min(m.sent_at)                                     AS first_at,
         max(m.sent_at)                                     AS last_at
  FROM chat_messages m
  JOIN targets t ON t.interaction_id = m.interaction_id
  GROUP BY m.interaction_id
)
UPDATE interactions i SET
  message_count          = agg.n_total,
  customer_message_count = agg.n_customer,
  agent_message_count    = agg.n_agent,
  started_at             = agg.first_at,
  ended_at               = agg.last_at,
  handled_by             = CASE WHEN agg.n_agent > 0 THEN 'agent'::speaker_role
                                ELSE i.handled_by END,
  updated_at             = now()
FROM agg
WHERE i.interaction_id = agg.interaction_id
-- first_response_seconds and is_after_hours stay NULL on purpose. Both are
-- rules, not counts: the response gap has to skip non-text turns, and
-- after-hours has to be read in PORTAL_TZ_OFFSET_HOURS rather than off the wall
-- clock. Both already live in evaluate/metrics.py, and a second implementation
-- in SQL is a second thing to keep in step. NULL means "not computed yet";
-- 0 would be a claim.
RETURNING i.interaction_id, i.external_id, i.external_deal_id,
          i.external_contact_id, i.message_count, i.customer_message_count,
          i.agent_message_count, i.started_at, i.ended_at;

nodes.name: Renumber and refresh counters
nodes.notes: Counters are recomputed from the stored rows, never accumulated from the payload — so they read the same after one delivery and after ten redeliveries of the same messages.

parameters.query:
-- Close the loop. Any raw_events row with processed_at NULL is a delivery that
-- landed and was never normalised — the partial index on (processed_at) makes
-- that the replay queue, and it is empty when everything is healthy.
--
-- process_error is NOT cleared: when the normaliser dropped some rows it wrote
-- down why, and "stored, minus these" is a state worth keeping.
UPDATE raw_events
   SET processed_at = COALESCE(processed_at, now())
 WHERE raw_id = $1::bigint
RETURNING raw_id, processed_at, process_error;

nodes.name: Mark raw processed
nodes.notes: raw_id comes back from Postgres as a STRING (bigint), which is why the query casts $1::bigint rather than trusting the type.
